candidate_label: Compact solid nodule separated from pleural boundaries
description: A compact, rounded to mildly lobulated solid nodule with a substantial soft-tissue core visible on mediastinal windows, surrounded by aerated lung rather than broadly merging with the pleura, chest wall, mediastinum or diaphragm. Margins are usually well defined; nearby thin vessels may touch the nodule without forming a broad soft-tissue attachment.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule separated from pleural surfaces
description: A compact, roughly rounded soft-tissue nodule lies within aerated lung, with a visible lung gap separating it from the chest wall and diaphragm across the views. Thin vessel connections may be present, but the nodule does not form a broad-based projection from a pleural surface; the low-response examples mostly show surface-attached opacities or less compact, strand-like densities.

candidate_label: Compact rounded rather than elongated or branching nodule
description: A compact, rounded or mildly ovoid nodule that remains relatively bulky in the coronal and sagittal planes, with much of its outline bordering aerated lung. Nearby thin vessels may touch it, but the main opacity is not predominantly elongated, tapered, triangular or branching, nor broadly merged with pleural soft tissue.

candidate_label: Compact rounded core with a convex posterior edge
description: The nodule has a compact, rounded or ovoid body, with a relatively full, convex posterior margin (bottom of the axial image and right side of the sagittal image). Thin attached strands may be present, but the central opacity is more blob-like than the predominantly angular, tapering, elongated or branching opacities common in the L images.

candidate_label: Compact solid nodule with a convex free margin
description: A discrete, compact, rounded or mildly lobulated solid nodule has a substantial convex margin directly bordering aerated lung. Small vessels or short strands may touch it, but the main opacity remains a recognizable nodular body rather than a long, tapering or branching structure.

candidate_label: Compact nodule with a convex image-right air border
description: The nodule has a filled-in, compact bright body with a convex right-hand edge against dark lung in the axial and coronal views. This contrasts with predominantly elongated, branching, flattened, or ring-shaped opacities; the relevant right-hand edge is not broadly continuous with adjacent dense tissue.

candidate_label: Nodule–aerated lung interface (nonspecific)
description: The nodules have a lung-facing edge bordered by aerated lung, often with small vessel-like markings or thin strands nearby. This appearance occurs in both groups; smooth versus irregular margins, pleural contact, and internal density do not consistently distinguish the high examples.

candidate_label: Possible lung-facing anterior nodule cap
description: Many H nodules have a rounded anterior-facing margin bordered by dark lung, visible at the top of the axial image and the left side of the sagittal image. However, this appearance also occurs in several L images, so it does not reliably distinguish the groups.

candidate_label: Nodule away from broad tissue boundaries
description: The nodule sits within aerated lung without a nearby broad pleural, diaphragmatic, chest-wall or mediastinal soft-tissue boundary. Nearby opacities are mainly thin vessels or small branching structures, rather than a broad tissue surface separated from the nodule by only a narrow strip of lung.

candidate_label: Nodule in relatively open lung
description: The nodule is surrounded by a relatively broad cuff of aerated lung across the three planes, with few bulky adjacent structures. Compared with the L examples, there is usually more separation from the chest wall, diaphragm, mediastinal soft tissue, or a crowded cluster of thick branching opacities.

candidate_label: Vessel-adjacent nodule margin (nonspecific)
description: The high examples show nodules surrounded by aerated lung, with small vessels or fine linear strands approaching, abutting, or blending into their margins. However, this same appearance is common in the low examples, and neither nodule contour nor internal density provides a consistent visible distinction.

candidate_label: Nodule set back from the lung boundary
description: The nodule lies within aerated lung, with a relatively broad gap between it and the nearest chest-wall, mediastinal, or diaphragmatic surface across the three planes. In contrast, most L nodules have a lung boundary noticeably closer in at least one plane.

candidate_label: Fine perinodular linear markings, not discriminatory
description: Thin linear or branching soft-tissue densities approach, abut, or traverse the nodule, with aerated lung between the markings. This appearance occurs in both groups, around both well-defined solid nodules and irregular opacities with hazy margins.

candidate_label: No consistent plain-CT pattern
description: Both groups contain compact, rounded bright nodules as well as irregular opacities with radiating strands or adjoining vessels. Nodule shape, internal brightness, and proximity to the pleural surface do not visibly separate the groups consistently.

candidate_label: Non-pleural nodule with fine vessel contacts (nonspecific)
description: High examples commonly show a nodule surrounded by aerated lung, without direct pleural attachment, with thin vessels or short linear strands approaching or contacting its margins. However, this same appearance occurs in many low examples and does not reliably distinguish the groups.

candidate_label: No consistent visible discriminator
description: Both groups contain compact, smooth round nodules and irregular or elongated opacities with thin linear extensions. Neither the nodule contour, visible vessel connections, nor proximity to the pleural surface consistently separates the H images from the L images.

candidate_label: Discrete bulky solid nodule with an exposed lower margin
description: A rounded or lobulated, bulky soft-tissue nodule remains distinguishable from contacting vessels and thin strands, with a substantial lower margin bordered by aerated lung on coronal and sagittal views. It is not predominantly a thin, tapering band or branching opacity, and its lower portion does not broadly blend into pleural or diaphragmatic soft tissue.

candidate_label: Bulky nodule with an air-exposed lower border
description: The opacity has a substantial rounded, lobulated or irregular nodular body in both coronal and sagittal views, with much of its lower border outlined by dark aerated lung. Unlike most L examples, it is not predominantly a thin elongated band, branching strand or broad opacity merging into the pleura or diaphragm.

candidate_label: Aerated-lung nodule margin away from pleura
description: The nodule lies predominantly within aerated lung rather than immediately beside a broad pleural, chest-wall or other soft-tissue boundary. Its superior margin is exposed to lung, often with a short tapered projection or contacting thin vessel-like strand, rather than forming part of a pleura-directed band.

candidate_label: Free upper nodule margin in aerated lung
description: The nodule has a distinct rounded, lobulated or pointed upper margin projecting into dark aerated lung, with open lung above and beside it in the coronal and sagittal views. It is generally more separate from broad pleural or chest-wall surfaces than the L examples, many of which are peripheral or predominantly thin and band-like.

candidate_label: Irregular solid–lung margin with short strands
description: The nodule has a dense, lobulated or angular outer contour with short tapering projections or thin soft-tissue strands extending into aerated lung. This contrasts with a predominantly smooth oval outline or a broad margin against pleural soft tissue; in cavitary examples, assess the outer wall rather than the internal air space.

candidate_label: Anterior tapering projection or strand
description: The nodule’s anterior edge has an angular, tapering projection or a bright strand extending into the adjacent lung, rather than a smoothly rounded contour. Look at the top of the nodule in the axial view and its left-facing edge in the sagittal view; the extension may merge with a nearby branching linear opacity.

candidate_label: No consistent distinguishing CT pattern
description: Both groups contain peripheral nodules with pleural contact or a narrow intervening rim of aerated lung, as well as nodules abutting small branching vessels. Smooth solid nodules, irregular opacities with linear extensions, and hazy opacities without a definite solid core occur in both groups.

candidate_label: No consistent plain-CT distinction
description: Both groups contain compact rounded nodules, irregular or branching opacities, and nodules touching or lying just inside the pleural surface. No consistent difference in contour, internal appearance, or attachment to nearby linear structures separates the H images from the L images.

candidate_label: Discrete lung-surrounded nodule
description: A rounded, ovoid or lobulated nodule is visibly separate from the pleura, chest wall and central hilar soft tissue, with aerated lung between them; thin vessels or strands may still contact its margins. The nodule forms a substantial, readily distinguishable body rather than a tiny vessel-like focus or an opacity broadly merging with adjacent soft tissue.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: The H images show a distinct rounded or irregular nodular opacity lying within aerated lung, with lung separating most of its outline from the chest wall or mediastinum. Thin connecting strands may be present, but the opacity is not simply a broad-based projection from an adjacent soft-tissue boundary; most L images instead show such boundary-attached projections or only a very faint, tiny focus.

candidate_label: Compact nodule with irregular, hazy margins (weak trend)
description: The high examples generally show a compact rounded-to-ovoid opacity with slightly irregular or indistinct margins and fine strands or small vessels meeting its edge, surrounded by aerated lung. This appearance is less bandlike or air-centred than some low examples, but is also present in several low examples.

candidate_label: Compact nodule with a fuzzy, tufted edge
description: The opacity forms a compact, roughly rounded focus with an uneven, softly fading edge and short wispy or pointed extensions into the surrounding lung. This contrasts with a sharply outlined smooth dot, a predominantly thin linear or branching opacity, or a hollow ring.

candidate_label: Basal or cardiomediastinal lung interface
description: The nodule lies in aerated lung immediately above the curved diaphragm or beside the cardiac/mediastinal soft-tissue border, often within a narrow strip of lung along that boundary. Proximity to the lateral or apical chest-wall pleura alone does not show the same association; nodule shape and internal density vary considerably.

candidate_label: Lung-base context near the diaphragm
description: The nodule lies in basal lung just above a broad, curved diaphragm boundary, most clearly visible on the coronal and sagittal views. The surrounding aerated lung often forms a shallow crescent or tapering wedge between this boundary and the chest wall.

candidate_label: Compact rounded nodule with a clean border
description: A compact round or ovoid nodule with a mostly smooth or gently lobulated, well-defined border against aerated lung and a largely uniform solid interior. It lacks the conspicuous tapered extensions, branching shape, radiating strands, blurred margins or large internal air space seen in many low examples.

candidate_label: Compact rounded nodule with smooth convex margins
description: The central opacity is a compact, filled-in round or oval shape, with predominantly smooth, outwardly convex borders in the three planes. It is not chiefly a thin band, branching or star-shaped opacity, or a ring surrounding a dark centre.

candidate_label: No consistent distinguishing plain-CT pattern
description: Both groups include solid lobulated nodules with short radiating strands, adjacent branching vessels, and contact with pleural or mediastinal soft tissue. Bulky rounded contours are more common among the high examples, but neither this shape nor a particular margin, internal air space, or attachment consistently separates the groups.

candidate_label: Broad upper-facing opacity margin
description: A relatively broad, well-defined upper surface of a dense opacity borders dark aerated lung, best seen in the coronal or sagittal view. This surface may be rounded, sloping or interrupted by short pointed projections; it is not merely a thin vertical strand or the downward-facing tip of an opacity attached above.

candidate_label: Compact rounded nodule with a clean lung interface
description: A compact round-to-oval solid nodule with a smooth or mildly lobulated, clearly defined contour against aerated lung. Unlike elongated, flattened or branching opacities, its main body remains readily distinguishable from nearby vessels, without prominent tapering extensions, radiating strands or a bandlike pleural connection.

candidate_label: Compact rounded nodule with convex margins
description: The central opacity is compact and round or oval in the axial and coronal views, with a well-defined, predominantly smooth outward-curving margin. A thin vessel may touch it, but the main opacity remains a distinct rounded body rather than an elongated band, branching shape, or angular opacity with long radiating extensions.

candidate_label: Discrete rounded nodule separated from pleural surfaces
description: A compact round or mildly oval, homogeneous solid-appearing nodule with a well-defined smooth to mildly lobulated outline, surrounded by aerated lung rather than broadly merging with pleural or diaphragmatic soft tissue. A narrow lung gap may separate it from a nearby surface, and fine vessels may approach its edge; it is not flattened, branching, wedge-shaped or predominantly hazy.

candidate_label: Discrete rounded nodule
description: A compact, well-defined round or oval opacity remains rounded across all three planes, with a substantial central body rather than a thin, branching, or plate-like shape. Most of its outline is bordered by dark lung, even when close to the chest wall; it does not broadly merge with the pleural surface.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule with aerated-lung clearance
description: A compact round or mildly lobulated nodule stands out as a discrete focus within aerated lung, with appreciable lung separating it from broad pleural, chest-wall, mediastinal or diaphragmatic soft-tissue boundaries. Small vessels may touch it, but its contour remains distinguishable rather than blending extensively into branching linear opacities.

candidate_label: Compact rounded nodule separated from pleural surfaces
description: The nodule is a compact round or ovoid focus with a convex upper outline on coronal and sagittal views, generally separated from the chest wall and diaphragm by a substantial band of dark lung. A thin vessel attachment may be present, but the focus is not predominantly a flattened, elongated, or branching opacity.

candidate_label: Peripheral nodular–bandlike junction
description: A peripheral opacity blends into tapering linear or branching soft-tissue strands, forming an angular, elongated, or bandlike complex near a pleural, diaphragmatic, or mediastinal boundary. Look for continuity between the nodular portion and adjoining bands rather than a separately outlined rounded nodule; pleural contact alone is not distinguishing.

candidate_label: Angular pleural tethering and band-like extensions
description: The nodule or adjacent opacity has thin, tapering linear extensions toward a nearby pleural surface or fissure, often producing a triangular, tented, or concave contour. This is more characteristic of the H images than a compact rounded nodule or a smooth, broad-based pleural bulge without conspicuous connecting bands.

candidate_label: Fine vessel adjoining a nodule margin (nonspecific)
description: Most high examples show a small rounded or mildly lobulated nodule with a fine linear vessel approaching, touching, or blending into one edge, surrounded by aerated lung. However, the same appearance is common in the low examples and does not consistently distinguish the groups.

candidate_label: Compact rounded contour (not consistently distinguishing)
description: Several H images show a compact round or ovoid nodule with a smooth convex margin, sometimes with a thin linear extension. However, this appearance also occurs in multiple L images, while some H nodules are elongated or angular.

candidate_label: Deeper intrapulmonary rather than chest-wall-adjacent location
description: The opacity lies deeper within the lung, away from the peripheral chest-wall pleural surface, with aerated lung bordering much of its contour and nearby branching vessels often meeting its margins. In contrast, the low examples predominantly occupy a narrow peripheral strip of lung close to, or directly against, the chest-wall pleura.

candidate_label: Coarse angular margins and thick tapering extensions
description: The nodule, cavity wall, or pleural-based opacity has a dense, sharply outlined margin with coarse angular projections, deep notches, or thick tapering extensions into adjacent lung. These are broader tissue tongues or branching attachments rather than only fine wispy spicules; the low-response examples more often have a smooth rounded outline or a faint, thin irregular margin.

candidate_label: No consistent plain-CT distinction
description: Both groups contain small rounded solid-appearing nodules in aerated lung, often beside small vessels or near the pleura, as well as larger irregular hazy opacities with internal strands and air spaces. Nodule shape, margin sharpness, vessel contact and pleural attachment do not consistently distinguish the groups.

candidate_label: No consistent distinguishing CT pattern
description: Both groups include small rounded nodules, irregular opacities with linear extensions, and nodules close to the pleural surface. No consistent difference in shape, margins, internal air spaces, or pleural relationship separates the H images from the L images.
